_comment: Baseline of tests/engine-invariants.html. Each value hashes that configuration's rounded KPI set; open the harness and treat any changed fingerprint on an unchanged configuration as a regression. __all hashes the whole set.
_caveat: The hash covers the WHOLE KPI object, so ADDING or RENAMING an output key - or changing what an existing one MEANS - changes every fingerprint even though no number moved. A wholesale change across unrelated configurations usually means that, not a regression. Confirm by extracting the previous engine (git show <prev>:src/calc.js), running both against the same inputs, and comparing only the keys that existed before. Beware case when filtering keys by regex: /horizonMonths/ does NOT match autoHorizonMonths.
_history: 860fe56 pre mixed-use. Mixed-use left all 34 fingerprints byte-identical. The debt-facility fix deliberately moved 29. Leasehold land added 5 KPI keys; a value-level diff confirmed zero freehold drift. Ground rent then moved to a monthly accrual, moving only the four leasehold fingerprints. Encumbered exit (leasehold NOI capitalised net of ground rent) added the annualRentAtExit key, re-hashing everything; a value-level diff over 300 numbers across 6 freehold configurations again confirmed zero drift, and leasehold exit values fell as intended. Ground rent was then found MISSING from totalCashCosts while present in grossCashflow - profit was overstated by the entire rent (83.2M vs 45.6M on a test scheme) while IRR was already correct, which is why it read as a high profit beside a modest return. Only the four leasehold fingerprints moved. Operating expenses then became a use so total uses equals total cost; no fingerprint moved.
_history2: The timeline was then re-cut to END on the last trading month: projectEndMonth switched from an exclusive to an inclusive convention, the three-month tail past the exit was dropped, and the exit moved from the month AFTER the hold onto its final month. Every fingerprint moves, because every horizon does - by four months (three of tail, one of boundary). A value-level diff against the previous engine confirmed the shape: revenue identical on all 48 configurations, and the only cost/profit movements are the four leasehold configurations, each falling by exactly one month of ground rent. Two consumers had latent off-by-ones that the tail had been absorbing: runWaterfall reads `horizon` as a month COUNT, and the operating loop clamps opEnd against `horizon` as if it were a count when it is a last index.
_history3: Purpose and basis toggles were then found to backfill a flipped unit's TIMING and operating assumptions but never its RATE, so a component switched to leasable had occupancy, an OpEx percentage and a cap rate but no rent - gross income zero, and OpEx being a percentage of it, zero too. It presented as 'OpEx only works on mixed-use', because a mixed-use space is created with a rate by addSub and so never took that path. Three near-duplicate backfills had drifted apart; they now share Feas.modeDefaults. No existing fingerprint moved - every pre-existing configuration states its own rates, so the backfill never fires on them - and five 'flipped:' configurations were added to cover the toggle paths.
_history4: minDSCR was then REPLACED by interestCover, which renames a KPI key and so re-hashes all 53 configurations. A value-level diff over the shared keys confirmed the swap is the whole story: 2650 values unchanged, 0 moved. The old ratio could not work in this model - the facility is a revolving sweep with no amortisation schedule, so 'debt service' was whatever cash the project happened to have, and the ratio only ever returned 0.00 (a month repaying out of previously retained cash, usually DURING CONSTRUCTION, so carrying no income of its own) or exactly 1.00 (the sweep taking the whole month's income). interestCover measures NOI net of ground rent against interest due, from stabilisation rather than handover, and is null - not zero - where the question does not apply.
_history5: autoHorizonMonths then moved by +1 on all 53 configurations, and that is the ONLY key that moved - no financial value changed anywhere. The timeline rework had left it returning the last month INDEX while its name, and every consumer that printed it, read it as a DURATION. A run from month 0 to month 83 lasts 84 months, so 24 months of predesign and construction plus a 60-month hold displayed as '83 months (6.9 yrs)' - a project a month shorter than its own inputs. Index and duration are now separate named quantities in runFeasibility (horizon vs horizonMonths), kpi.horizonMonths and kpi.autoHorizonMonths are both durations, and runWaterfall no longer needs its + 1. A pinned horizon is a duration too and was being compared against an index, so a pinned 120 quietly produced 121 months; pinned configurations are now exactly as long as typed, which changed no KPI because the extra month was empty.
_history6: The preferred return then began compounding on the whole UNRETURNED BALANCE - unreturned capital plus preferred return accrued and unpaid - instead of on capital alone. Only the six ::waterfall fingerprints move; project KPIs are untouched (0 moved, 2703 unchanged), because this is a distribution rule and changes no project cashflow. The fault it fixes: the waterfall returns capital before it pays preferred return, so on a hold the capital trickles back out of operating cash while the preferred return waits for the exit. Accruing on capital alone stopped the clock as capital was repaid, the preferred balance then sat for years earning nothing (35.4M accrued by month 73, unpaid until month 107), and settling it at face value emptied the bucket - so the hurdle test 'is any preferred return outstanding?' said cleared and released the promote to a fund that had returned 7.4% against an 8% hurdle. Compounding the whole balance makes it behave like a loan at the preferred rate, so it reaches zero if and only if the investor truly achieved that rate. On 'equity funded, lease only' the promote correctly falls from 2,856,149 to zero; where the hurdle IS met the promote shrinks because more cash now settles preferred return first.
_history7: The asset-management fee then gained its missing first month. The capital call was applied at the BOTTOM of the month loop while the fee was charged at the top, so month 0 saw paid-in capital of zero and charged nothing - the first year billed 11 months, 91K against 100K a year thereafter, and every fund was short exactly one month over its whole life (107 of 108, 49 of 50). The call now precedes the fee it is charged on, and amLoad moved from horizon - 1 to horizon so equityAtClose still covers the fees levied on it; the self-funding gap is zero on every fund configuration. Only the ::waterfall fingerprints move - 0 of 2703 project KPI values changed - because this is a fee-timing rule and touches no project cashflow. An invariant now asserts fees.assetMgmt equals equityAtClose x rate/12 x fundLifeMonths exactly, which fails on the previous engine for all seven fee-charging configurations.
